title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Wednesday, October 14th | Press Conference
headline: Michael Penix Jr. is limited in practice but is expected to start Sunday if he progresses; C.J. Henderson sat Wednesday but is not ruled out for the Bears game.
summary: Stefanski said the Falcons begin preparation for the Bears on Wednesday. Michael Penix Jr. will be limited in some fashion, with his rep count to be decided after talking with him, and he is expected to start Sunday as long as things go to plan. Za'Darius Smith is working back from a neck injury and will be monitored over the next few days with treatment. C.J. Henderson will not practice Wednesday but is improving and is not being ruled out for the game. Stefanski described Chicago as an excellent team and praised Ben Johnson and coordinator Dennis Allen's defense, which is aggressive with press-man, edge pressure, and a mix of coverages. He said the week's focus is learning Chicago's schemes and the individual matchups. On the offensive line, he credited Bill Callahan and the group's routine and continuity, and said the wide zone run game has long been a strength, with some adjustments in how it is run. He also praised rookie Kendal Daniels for handling a heavy, multi-position workload, including linebacker and end reps. Avieon Terrell is getting better and has played both inside and outside.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears' Week 6 mindset | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Williams's Week 6 status is still fluid, Austin Booker is gaining snaps, and Dayo Odeyingbo is expected to miss some time after going down in the Green Bay game.
summary: Johnson said Wednesday's walk-through was a planned mid-season reset before the bye, and he framed Atlanta as a strong team in all three phases and a tough road test. He confirmed the Montez Sweat suspension, said he was not aware of an appeal, and said Sweat's absence is next-man-up. Dayo Odeyingbo went down in the Green Bay game; the coach said he will likely miss some time, though not enough to go on IR, and that defensive linemen who were active in camp may get opportunities. Johnson described Austin Booker as trending up in snaps and production, and said Shemar Turner's return to the 53-man roster helps. He said Tyrique Stevenson is more day-to-day and T.J. Edwards is more week-to-week. On the quarterback spot, he said Caleb Williams is expected to be full in practice, but the Sunday decision is still fluid and based on what is best for winning. He took responsibility for the offense's struggles and said health is the top priority for all the quarterbacks. On the backfield, he said the team will use running back by committee and will not lean on one back for 50-plus snaps. He said the offense must return to fundamentals, cut down on volume and three-and-outs, and clean up turnovers and explosive plays. On Kyler Gordon, he said the team is considering all options but the plan was to use the full 21-day window.

title: Shane Steichen: Midweek update, Colts vs. Titans
headline: Josh Downs and Tyler Warren are leading the target share, with Jonathan Taylor's breakout still hinging on execution; Will Mallory's status is still being evaluated.
summary: Steichen opened by calling the home division game against Tennessee important and said the team is glad to be back at Lucas Oil Stadium. He said the veteran linebacker signed to the practice squad (the transcript spells him 'Jermaine,' likely Germaine Pratt) will be brought up to speed this week, and Steichen declined to say whether he can play Sunday. On Josh Downs, he said defenses have been doubling him on third down, so the staff needs to find the single coverage and move him around. He said Tyler Warren's big numbers are part of a rotating target picture that will even out over the season, and he is not concerned about the other receivers yet at five games. On Jonathan Taylor, Steichen said the offense needs better execution against stacked fronts and wants the explosive chunk runs back that it had last year. He said Will Mallory is still being evaluated this week and denied the Pratt signing was related to any injury. He also said Darius Slayton's knee is improving, and he flagged red-zone efficiency and turnovers as the main areas to fix.

title: Coen on "Next Man Up" Mentality, Red Zone Execution & WR Marvin Harrison Jr. | Press Conference
headline: Tackle out for a game after a procedure, Eric Murray (limited) and Trevor Lawrence's improving pocket play are the fantasy watch items for the Houston game.
summary: Coen said the injured tackle will have a procedure after the team returns and that there is no clear timeline yet, so they will take it day by day. He has confidence in Walker Little and Cole Van Lanen to replace him, with a next-man-up mindset. On Houston, he expects a physical test: their run defense is strong, they play more man coverage at times, and their record doesn't change how he views them. He praised C.J. Stroud for getting the ball out on time, scrambling more, and making contested-catch throws with his receivers. Coen said the offense must execute better in the red zone, admitted some self-inflicted mistakes and play-call issues, and said the offense held a candid meeting on Monday. He praised Trevor Lawrence's improved movement in the pocket and throwing on the run, and said the fourth-down touchdown to Parker Washington came from a slot fade. Eric Murray has not been able to do much since last week, and Coen will see how he moves today and tomorrow. Josh Cameron has been impressive on special teams and as a blocker. Kaevon Merriweather was elevated to help special teams, with a long snapper and the Ross timeline factored in.

title: Andy Reid on Chargers: 'They Play Hard and They're Well Coached' | Press Conference 10/14
headline: Rashee Rice won't practice Wednesday, and Tyquan Thornton's injury opens a larger role for the remaining receivers, with Xavier Worthy named as a key target.
summary: Reid said Rashee Rice (transcribed as 'Rasheed') was the only injured player who would not practice Wednesday, while everyone else had some level of work scheduled. He said the team is preparing for the Chargers, whom he described as well coached and playing hard despite their record, and noted they are largely the same group that beat KC last year. Reid addressed Tyquan Thornton's injury, saying he was sad to see it happen and that the loss creates an opportunity for whoever steps in. He said he has trusted the rest of the receivers, including Xavier Worthy, who has made some good catches recently. On the bye week, Reid said it came earlier than he could remember, and he described his routine as largely unchanged, with the film review process the same as any week. He cited short-yardage execution as an area needing improvement. Reid also said the team rotates its fourth and fifth receivers in practice so they're ready when needed. The transcript is garbled, so some player references (a player returning to limited practice with a hamstring issue, a lineman's role, and a player working out with trainers) could not be reliably matched to the roster and were left out.

title: Sean McVay breaks down special teams changes, takeaways from Bills matchup, preparing for Week 6 & more
headline: Alaric Jackson is suspended for two games and David Quessenberry takes over at left tackle; Kyren Williams's receiving role keeps growing.
summary: McVay said left tackle Alaric Jackson was suspended two games for a punch and that he learned of it only that morning. Jackson plans to appeal, and McVay said he will keep the discipline matter internal. David Quessenberry will fill the spot, and Trost clock is expected back this week. McVay said special teams needs more consistency, that he has confidence in coordinator Bubba Ventrone, and that no changes are coming there. He took accountability for a late-game decision, the choice to go for it instead of kicking, which ended in a failed attempt. He also addressed the 42 penalties in five games, mostly pre-snap procedural flags, and said he expects the trend to be a blip. On offense, Kyren Williams has been a late checkdown and primary target and is now tied for the NFL lead in receptions by a running back. Matthew Stafford was praised for his two-minute operation and progression reads. Davante Adams is expected to keep improving after missing much of camp. The team came out of the game largely healthy.

title: Jim Harbaugh on Khalil Mack's Mentorship of Akheem Mesidor
headline: Chargers' Cole Strange looks ready to return Sunday, while Khalil Mack (about two weeks out) and several others remain sidelined; RB Omarion Hampton's snap decline is worth watching.
summary: Harbaugh gave a broad injury update: several players did not practice, including KeAndre Lambert-Smith, Derwin James, Donte Jackson, Rodney Shelley, and Khalil Mack, who has been out close to two weeks and is working to return. He said Cole Strange, who was playing well before his injury, seems ready to go and that he is looking forward to watching practice. He said the bye-week timing helps players who are working through something. The team badly needs a first win, and Harbaugh said the staff is working harder and smarter to get there. He praised Akheem Mesidor and Khalil Mack's mentorship and said both are playing high-level football, with Mesidor and Mack feeding off each other. On Omarion Hampton, Harbaugh praised him in all phases but did not explain why his snaps have dropped for a third straight week, saying he doesn't focus on carry counts. He called Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell outstanding backs as well. Harbaugh said Justin Herbert has responded impressively to adversity and that the leaders, including Mack, Derwin James, and Herbert, have not let up in setting the tone. He also said the team signed a practice-squad receiver after a workout and that the receiver room is now set. Harbaugh praised Kenneth Walker and the Chiefs' rushing effectiveness, and said the team will face a tall task against Patrick Mahomes.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 14, 2026
headline: Landon Dickerson's activation off injured reserve is expected to be announced later today; Sirianni gave no timeline for Eli Stowers and no clear answer on Dickerson's starting spot.
summary: Sirianni said the Eagles will share information later on Wednesday about whether Landon Dickerson will be activated, and that the team is still working through some decisions. He praised Dickerson's work ethic and body care during his recovery, but declined to say whether Dickerson would return to left guard, citing the time before decisions must be made. Asked why Eli Stowers was eligible to come off injured reserve last week, Sirianni said players are activated when they are ready and that he doesn't discuss injuries in detail. On Jalen Hurts, he said the run game is part of the plan only some weeks and that Hurts' passing, scrambling, and designed runs all remain options. He called Bryce Young a much-improved quarterback who processes quickly, gets the ball out fast, and keeps his eyes downfield when he escapes pressure, and said the Panthers are a solid team. He described Carolina's defense as active and singled out two standouts the Eagles must track on every play, without naming them. On the analytics and fourth-down questions, he said decisions weigh analytics alongside players, past experience and game context, and that the Eagles need to improve their short-yardage play design and execution. He also said the Eagles are open to anything, including Sean moving down to the field to call plays, though he gave no commitment. Finally, he said a player on the injury list has been working hard to return, that the setback did not change expectations for him, and that he is looking forward to his return.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Gives Final Updates Ahead Of Week 6 at Broncos
headline: Drake Thomas is out for Week 6 at Denver, Tyrice Knight steps in on defense, Zach Charbonnet is not playing, and Irvin Charles is back from IR with special-teams value.
summary: Mike Macdonald said the team is doubling down on how it handles adversity: attacking problems, finding solutions, evolving, and having each other's backs, a lesson he especially wants newer players to learn from losses. He said Drake Thomas is out for this game and would not say whether the absence extends beyond it, calling him a tough player. He expects Tyrice Knight, who is replacing Thomas, to play well and said the defensive standard stays the same. Macdonald said Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Leonard Williams look ready to play despite the short week. Zach Charbonnet looks great in practice but will not play this game, and Macdonald said the team is still working through how to handle his return from a knee injury. He called Bo Nix impressive, noting his playmaking, his ability to change plays, and his command of tempo and the operation. On Denver's offense, he said the staff has had little crossover tape with them since last year, so it is still learning the scheme and how newly added Jaylen Waddle lines up alongside Courtland Sutton. Macdonald also said Irvin Charles, activated off IR, is a strong special-teams player who could help on offense in a limited role, with his opportunity coming when it arrives.

title: Todd Bowles on Bucky Irving: ‘Determined to Win’ | Press Conference
headline: Jalon Daniels and Bucky Irving are trending up with Bowles praising their command and drive, while Baker Mayfield's status for Sunday is still unresolved and Sean Tucker is dealing with a quad issue.
summary: Bowles gave no new update on Baker Mayfield, saying he is getting better but that his throwing and health will be evaluated in that afternoon's session, and he would not commit to a plan until Mayfield threw. He said a healthy starter makes the week simpler to prepare for, but any quarterback who isn't at 100% shouldn't play. On Jalon Daniels, Bowles credited his command in the huddle, getting the offense to the line on time, and seeing the game clearly, and said the game has slowed down for him after two starts. He praised Bucky Irving's hunger and determination and said the running game's success is a formula the team wants to build on each week. Sean Tucker is dealing with a quad issue, with a decision to come after Friday's practice. Bowles also highlighted A'Shawn Robinson as a central leader for the run defense and Keionte Scott as one of the team's best players this year. He said Tykee Smith took on some of Antoine Winfield Jr.'s duties and has handled them well. Looking ahead to Pittsburgh, he described Aaron Rodgers as elite in football IQ, accuracy, and anticipation, and called the Steelers' front smart and technically sound.

topics.detail: Bowles called Aaron Rodgers a nightmare to face because of his football IQ, accuracy, and pre-snap reads. He also said the Steelers' defensive front is smart and technically sound, which will challenge the offensive line.
Bowles praised Jaylen Warren as a complete back and described the Steelers' tight ends as versatile players who both run and block well, which the defense must account for.
Bowles credited the team's pattern of developing young players who can play multiple roles, including nickel, and said the ability to swap positions helps the secondary's versatility.
Bowles said teams can still improve tackling during the regular season through drills and wrap-up work, even with limits on padded practices.
